subject: hummingbird
title: What If You Had a Hummingbird's Metabolism? You'd Starve by Dinner

scenes.text: What if your body ran like a hummingbird's? You'd be starving by dinner.
Your heart jumps from about 70 beats a minute to over 1,200. You breathe around 250 times a minute, just sitting still.
A hummingbird's metabolism runs roughly 77 times faster than yours. To keep up, you'd need about 155,000 calories a day. That's a meal every few minutes.
Your blood sugar would sit at levels a doctor calls a diabetic emergency, because the sugar you swallow has to reach your muscles within minutes.
Skip food for a few hours and you run out of fuel entirely. So every night you'd do what hummingbirds do: shut down.
Heart slowed to a crawl, body cooled by 20 degrees or more, barely alive until sunrise. Not living fast. Just surviving until breakfast.

description:
What if you had a hummingbird's metabolism? Hummingbird hearts beat over 1,200 times a minute and they breathe about 250 times a minute at rest. Their metabolism runs roughly 77 times faster than a human's, so a person with the same engine would need around 155,000 calories a day and would carry blood sugar levels that would be a medical emergency in a human.
Because they burn fuel so fast, hummingbirds can starve within hours. To survive the night they enter torpor, slowing the heart and dropping body temperature from about 40 degrees Celsius to 20 or lower; one Andean species has been measured at 3.3 degrees.

first_comment: The black metaltail hummingbird of the Andes cools to 3.3 degrees Celsius on cold nights, the lowest body temperature ever measured in a bird or non-hibernating mammal. Which animal's body would you borrow for a day?
